purpose: Abrocitinib is used to treat moderate-to-severe eczema (atopic dermatitis) in adults and teenagers 12 years and older when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps reduce the itching, redness, and skin irritation caused by eczema. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other eczema treatments.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes overreacts and causes inflammation that leads to eczema flares. Abrocitinib works by blocking a specific protein in your body called JAK1, which acts like a signal that tells your immune system to cause that inflammation. By blocking this signal, the medication helps calm down your immune system and reduce the itching and rash.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headache, diarrhea, acne or pimples, cold sores or other cold-like symptoms, dizziness, and low platelet counts in your blood. Some people may also notice an increase in blood fats (cholesterol). Most side effects are mild and often get better over time.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious infections, including tuberculosis (TB), so your doctor will test you for TB before you start. It may increase the risk of blood clots, certain cancers, and serious heart problems, especially in older adults or those who smoke. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm your baby. Avoid live vaccines while taking this medicine. Your doctor will monitor your blood counts regularly while you are on this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 100 mg taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 200 mg once daily if needed. Take it with or without food, at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose, in which case just skip the missed one.
